rulings.Case Title: CONSERVATORSHIP OF CONNIE M. MARATAS
rulings.Calendar Matter: ADDED TO CALENDAR FOR Status Of Accounting
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. 1. Lack of Transferee for Remaining Conservatorship Assets. a) The conservatee died on 1/9/24 with assets in the conservatorship estate that would be subject to formal probate proceedings. A personal representative must be appointed to receive the assets remaining in this conservatorship estate. [LRSF 14.47 F.3.] b) The custodian of a will is required to lodge it with the clerk of the superior court of the county in which the estate of the decedent may be administered. [Probate Code Section 8200(a).] c) Niece Madeline Mulky mentioned at the hearing on 10/27/25 that the original will dated 11/19/24 was given to the APS social worker, along with the 2014 trust, by attorney Peter Clerides on 12/14/15. Additionally, a copy of the 2014 trust was attached to the initial petition filed in the related trust case on 10/28/19. 2. Contempt: If the conservator is unable or unwilling to continue serving as a fiduciary, the Court might wish to suspend or remove her and appoint a temporary successor fiduciary (possibly the Public Guardian or a private professional fiduciary) to wrap up the administration of this conservatorship estate. [Probate Code Sections 2620.2(b), 2650(c), and 2655.] 3. Impediment to Closing Trust Administration: Until this second and final accounting and the accounting subsequent to the date of death are filed, the related trust accounting cannot proceed, as the accounting periods overlap. These inordinate delays, furthermore, are a waste of the Court's resources and not in the best interests of the remainder beneficiaries. Please have the CASE NUMBER and the CASE NAME ready for the clerk. Parties appearing must check in for the hearing using their FULL NAME. Counsel and parties may appear in person or remotely through Zoom or CourtCall. Please review LRSF 14.1 D. for information on remote appearances. For Zoom appearance: meeting ID is 160 225 4765 and password is 514879. For audio-only telephone appearance via Zoom, call 1-669-254-5252 and follow the prompts, using the meeting ID and password above. rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF LIANA M LYMAN
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Accounting #1, Report, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 8/19/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) When an accounting is presented, original bank or brokerage statements must be filed to verify the ending balance(s) shown in the accounting. None appears to have been filed. [LRSF 14.34 D.] See CRC 7.575(b) for computer-generated printouts. (2) A petition for final distribution must state specifically how the estate is to be distributed... including... the net amount of cash (as of a date certain) distributable to each beneficiary. [CRC 7.651; LRSF 14.35 I.6.] (3) Reimbursements to an individual (especially to the fiduciary) must clearly identify the original payee and describe the disbursement. [LRSF 14.35 B.] (4) Why was Christine O'Bannon paid for the care of the decedent's dog? Did she adopt the dog or was that just for temporary care? The will requests that the SPCA care for any animal the decedent may own at the time of her death and that "the pet be... provided food and medical attention for the rest of his or her life." Please provide courtesy copies of any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 8/7/26. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B.

rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE PATRICIA PARKER TRUST
rulings.Calendar Matter: Petition For Order Determining Title To Personal Property
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 9/14/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) Prob. C. Sect. 850 is a shortcut for a formal probate proceeding. A beneficiary of the trust receives mailed notice with a copy of the petition, but any heir-at-law, who would stand to inherit, if the trust did not exist or were invalid, is a party whose right, title or interest would be affected by this petition, and, therefore, must receive (or waive) personal service of notice. [Prob. C. Sect. 17203(b) and CCP Sect. 413.10 et seq.] (2) In a supplement to the petition, signed and verified by the petitioner, all of the settlor's heirs-at-law must be identified and their last known addresses set forth. (If sisters (no brothers?) are the nearest kin, who were Decedent's parents and when did they die?) (3) The trust itself, furthermore, gives 25% to "the Sisters of Patricia Parker" but does not identify them, and Valerie (not "Valorie" as in the trust) Chappel is included in paragraph 12 of the petition as a sister. (4) Notice must be given directly to a person entitled to notice, not in care of another, unless the person entitled to notice is an adult and has directed the party giving notice in writing to send the notice in care of the second person. [CRC 7.51(a).] (5) Did the settlor not leave a will? Paragraph 11 seems to indicate that, if the relief were not granted, the accounts would pass by intestacy. (6) The Fidelity account appears to be "Y88," etc., not "488," etc. Please provide courtesy copies of all papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 8/31/26. NB: Notice of the supplement (or amendment, if the petition is amended) must be given in the same manner as the petition: 30 days' mailed notice to trust beneficiaries and by personal service on any heir-at-law who is not a trust beneficiary. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B.
